title: Transformation of Chemically Competent (Smart) Cells
author: Moriah Beck
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ssfeebn

steps.title: Thaw Competent Cells
steps.instruction: Remove cells from the –80 °C freezer and place them directly into an ice bucket to thaw for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Add DNA to Cells
steps.instruction: Add the plasmid DNA to the cells without mixing or stirring, as the cells are fragile.

substeps.instruction: For ligations/PCR products: use 10uL of ligation reaction per 50-100uL of cells
For purified plasmid (miniprep): use 1 uL of plasmid per aliquot of cells

steps.title: Incubate DNA and Prepare Heat Bath
steps.instruction: Incubate the cells with the DNA on ice for 30 minutes while ensuring a 42°C water bath or heat block is ready and filled with water.

steps.title: Heat Shock Cells
steps.instruction: Immerse the tube of cells in the 42°C bath for 45-60 seconds.

steps.title: Recover Cells on Ice
steps.instruction: Remove the tube from the water bath and place it directly on ice for 2 minutes to recover.

steps.title: Outgrowth Period
steps.instruction: Add 900 uL of sterile LB (without antibiotics) and grow the culture with shaking for 1 hour at 37 °C.

steps.title: Plate Cells
steps.instruction: Plate the cells onto the appropriate antibiotic selective plate using one of the following methods based on the DNA amount:

substeps.instruction: Standard: Plate out 50-200 uL directly onto the antibiotic selective plate

For cloning (small amounts of DNA): Spin cells in a tabletop centrifuge for 1 minute at ~2,000 rpm, remove 700uL of media, resuspend the cell pellet in the remaining media, and plate onto the correct antibiotic LB plate
